title: Forming comparatives and superlatives
intro: Read this before the questions. The form depends on the NUMBER OF SYLLABLES of the adjective.

blocks.title: the main rules
items: **Three or more syllables:** use **more** / **most**: beautiful, **more beautiful**, **the most beautiful**.
**Two syllables ending in -y:** change y to **-ier** / **-iest**: happy, **happier**, **the happiest**.
**Other two-syllable adjectives:** usually **more** / **most** (careful, modern, boring). A few take both (quiet, clever, simple, narrow).

blocks.title: building the sentence
items: **Comparing two things:** comparative + **than**: She is **taller than** her sister. This book is **more interesting than** that one.
**The top of three or more:** **the** + superlative + in / of: He is **the oldest** boy **in** the class. It was **the best** of the three.
**Equal:** as + basic adjective + as: Anna is **as tall as** Ben.

blocks.title: the slips
items: **No double comparatives:** more taller and most easiest are wrong. Say taller, easiest.
The superlative needs **the**: the tallest, not tallest.
Use **in** with a place or group (in the class, in the world) and **of** with a number of things (of the three).
